descriptor.scene: Night. Maya sits small in the lower left at a tiny camp: a low fire, a bedroll, her closed laptop on her knees under her folded hands, firelight warm on her thinking face. Above and to the right, filling most of the frame, floats one large SOFT PAINTED THOUGHT BUBBLE with a gently scalloped edge, its interior a warm cream vignette: inside it, two anonymous founders stand close together in painterly softness, one leaning to the other's ear, hand cupped, whispering, while pointing toward a tiny warm glow between distant painted trees. The bubble's content is the answer she is arriving at: not a myth, not a stage, a friend leaning close. The fire keeps the lower left warm; the lower right stays calm dark ferns.
descriptor._caption: That night Maya counts every founder she has ever known who made it up. Not one of them found their elevator in a myth or an announcement. Each one had a friend who found it and told them first, quietly, the same hour. Finders tell their friends.

MAYA: a founder, half-Black and half-white, in her sage-olive single-button notch-lapel blazer with the sleeves pushed to the elbow, plain WHITE crew-neck tee, STONE KHAKI chinos (never blue jeans, never denim trousers), white sneakers, and a closed silver laptop carried under her left arm. Identity of record; wardrobe and features exactly as the locked sheets. the-jungle exactly as its reference plate: A vast emerald wilderness of giant-leafed trees, buttress roots, hanging lianas and layered green depth, crossed by narrow hand-cut trails. No ruins, no temples, no animals with screen presence, no signage, no lettering anywhere. The trees are cathedral-tall: a standing adult reaches roughly the height of a buttress root's shoulder, and the canopy closes far overhead. Trails are one person wide. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
